sections.h2: Who handles real estate records in Paulding County?
sections.html:
Paulding County's recorder files and preserves the land documents for the county, such as deeds, mortgages and easements. Its desk is inside the courthouse at 115 N. Williams Street, Paulding, the village that also serves as county seat.

On the recorder's website the records search stays available all day and night, and the office says it is free of direct charges. Drafting is outside its job: if a deed still has to be written, ask the attorney or title agent on your sale.

The county is lightly settled. Census estimates for July 2025 show 18,727 people on roughly 416 square miles of land, about 45 per square mile.

sections.h2: How does a deed get recorded in Paulding County?
sections.html:
Usually the closing agent takes care of it, and the seller never touches the deed again. Anyone doing it personally has two stops: the auditor transfers the parcel on the tax list, and then the recorder files the instrument.

Three electronic recording vendors are listed on the recorder's site: CSC, ePN and Simplifile. The listing states that eRecording submissions are taken on weekdays between 8:00 am and 3:00 pm.

Look over the deed before anyone signs it:

  • The signature has to be acknowledged before an officer named in Revised Code 5301.01, and that officer certifies the acknowledgment.
  • It should name the new owner's mailing address for tax bills and cite the prior recorded instrument, both of which the auditor uses under section 319.20.
  • Its layout should follow the state's margin and type rules, or a surcharge is added.

sections.h2: What does the Paulding County recorder charge?
sections.html:
Ohio's recorder association lists the statewide base as $34.00 for a deed or mortgage's opening two pages, then $8.00 for every page following. On top of that, a county can tack on a preservation surcharge as high as $5.00 per document, and counties choose their own amount. Phone the recorder for the exact total before writing the check.

Typical Ohio recording charges (Ohio Recorders Association fee page; Revised Code 317.32)
ChargeAmount
Deed or mortgage, pages one and two$34.00
Every page beyond two$8.00
Layout does not meet state standards$20.00 more
Release or other paper needing a reference$4.00 more per reference
County preservation surchargeUp to $5.00

The extra $20 reaches documents prepared after June 30, 2009 that miss the standards. Those call for type of at least 10 points, black or blue ink only, a 3 inch blank band at the top of the first page, and 1 inch margins at the sides and bottom.

sections.h2: What should a Paulding County seller review before signing?
sections.html:
A few minutes of review can head off a rejected filing.

  • Match the seller's name to the way it appears on the last recorded deed. If it differs, explain the difference in the deed or an affidavit.
  • Collect the lender's payoff letter. A recorded release normally follows the payoff.
  • Have the buyer's complete tax mailing address in hand for the auditor's tax list.
  • When only a piece of a tract is being sold, ask the auditor and engineer whether the new description needs sign-off, since each Ohio county adopts its own conveyance standards.
  • Prepare a check for the precise conveyance fee. Paulding's auditor warns that any other amount stalls the transfer.

Closing attorneys and title agents normally cover all of these. Even in a fast cash sale the same items apply, so settle them well ahead of closing day.

sections.h2: What fees does the Paulding County auditor collect on a sale?
sections.html:
Before the deed reaches the recorder, the auditor takes two charges. The auditor's website lists the conveyance fee at $4.00 per thousand of the purchase price and a transfer fee of $.50 per parcel.

The auditor also cautions that a check has to equal the conveyance fee exactly, or the conveyance is held up. A conveyance calculator sits under the Tools menu on that site, so run your own price through it.

Section 319.202(D) puts the cost on the seller. The standard sale goes with form DTE 100, and anyone claiming an exemption uses DTE 100 (EX). Ask the auditor about extra steps when the sale includes mineral rights or a manufactured home.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Paulding County housing?
sections.html:
Paulding County leans heavily toward homeownership. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates give these numbers for the county.

  • Share of homes lived in by their owners: 80.1%.
  • Typical value of an owner's home: $140,800.
  • Typical gross rent: $812 monthly.
  • Households: 7,624, at 2.45 people each.
  • Housing units counted on July 1, 2025: 8,597.
  • Permits for new buildings in 2025: 28.

Twenty-eight permits across eleven villages and the farm townships is a small count, and the Census reports 90.6% of residents living at the same address a year earlier.

sections.h2: How big is the Paulding County economy?
sections.html:
Employers numbered 309 in 2023 and together had 4,033 jobs, 2.6% fewer than in 2022. About 62.6% of residents 16 and older are in the labor force, and a trip to work averages 24.0 minutes.

Business receipts in 2022 were roughly $56.0 million in transportation and warehousing, $50.4 million in health care and social assistance, and $137.3 million in retail. Household income in 2020 to 2024 had a midpoint of $67,731, and 10.4% of people live below the poverty line.

A home value of $140,800 sits well under Perry County's $191,100 and Pickaway County's $256,800 in the same Census table.

sections.h2: Which communities make up Paulding County?
sections.html:
Eleven villages dot the county: Antwerp, Broughton, Cecil, Grover Hill, Haviland, Latty, Melrose, Oakwood, Paulding, Payne and Scott. Students attend Antwerp Local, Paulding Exempted Village or Wayne Trace Local schools, and Vantage Career Center draws from the area.

Wikipedia calls the terrain extremely flat: the whole county sits in the former Great Black Swamp, and section roads run at one-mile spacing. U.S. Routes 127, 24 and 30 cross it, along with the Auglaize and Maumee rivers.

If a farm parcel is divided, the auditor will not transfer the new piece until its description has been reviewed. Check first with the auditor and the county engineer.

sections.h2: How can you look up a deed or mortgage release in Paulding County?
sections.html:
Start with the records search on the recorder's website, which connects to an Ava portal. That site also offers a property fraud alert and a notary fraud alert sign-up that send a notice when a document goes on record under a name you register.

A repaid mortgage appears as a recorded release. If you cannot recall whether a past loan was released, check before you list, because an open mortgage in the records turns up at closing.

Title companies and investors order the search regardless, so having the old deed and any release at hand saves time.

Heirs sometimes find a recorded document they do not recognize, such as an old easement or a lease. Copy its volume and page or instrument number from the search results so the title agent can read the whole instrument, then ask the recorder's office if the index entry is unclear.

faqs.q: Where does Paulding County file its land records?
faqs.a: At the recorder's office inside the courthouse at 115 N. Williams Street, Paulding, Ohio. The recorder's website also hosts the records search.

faqs.q: Is electronic recording available in Paulding County?
faqs.a: Yes. Documents can come through CSC, ePN or Simplifile on weekdays from 8:00 am to 3:00 pm.

faqs.q: What is Paulding County's conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The auditor's site gives it as $4.00 per thousand of the purchase price, with a $.50 transfer fee for each parcel. The calculator on the auditor's site does the math for your price.

faqs.q: Will the recorder draft my deed?
faqs.a: No, the recorder only records. An attorney or title company has to prepare the document.

faqs.q: Why was I charged an extra $20 on a deed?
faqs.a: Revised Code 317.114 sets that non-standard document charge for papers that break the margin, ink or type size rules. Check the layout against the standards before you sign.
